lq.ANSWER: Respect means right evaluation of a human being. Right evaluation must be based on the Self, not only on the body, wealth, post, marks, caste, gender or physical appearance. Respect includes right evaluation of intention and competence. Wrong evaluation may be of three types: over-evaluation, under-evaluation and otherwise-evaluation. All these are forms of disrespect because they do not evaluate the person as they really are. The minimum content of respect is to understand that the other is similar to me. Both I and the other want continuous happiness and prosperity; both of us have the same basic program of understanding and living in harmony; and both of us have the potential for right understanding. Therefore, respect means seeing the other as a human being like me, while also recognising differences in competence without disrespecting the person.
